title: Comparing Decimals and Decimals on a Number Line
seo_title: Grade 4 Comparing Decimals and Number Lines Worksheets (TEKS 4.2F, 4.2H, STAAR)
standard_text: 4.2F compare and order decimals using concrete and visual models to the hundredths; 4.2H determine the corresponding decimal to the tenths or hundredths place of a specified point on a number line; 4.3G represent fractions and decimals to the tenths or hundredths as distances from zero on a number line
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 worksheets for Texas TEKS 4.2F, 4.2H and 4.3G: decimals and fractions on number lines, compare and order decimals to hundredths, and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Line up the decimal points and compare from the left.
key_sub: Write 0.5 as 0.50 to compare with hundredths. On a number line, a decimal is a distance from 0.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • To compare decimals, line up the decimal points and compare place by place from the left: ones, tenths, hundredths.
  • Write a zero so both have hundredths: 0.5 = 0.50, so 0.5 > 0.45.
  • On a number line, count the equal spaces between 0 and 1: 10 spaces are tenths, 100 are hundredths. A point's decimal is its distance from 0.

Examples

Example

Compare 0.6 and 0.58.

0.6 = 0.60

60 hundredths > 58 hundredths

Answer: 0.6 > 0.58

Example

Order 0.4, 0.37, 0.09 from least to greatest.

0.40, 0.37, 0.09 in hundredths

Answer: 0.09, 0.37, 0.4

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Thinking 0.45 > 0.5 because 45 > 5Write 0.5 as 0.50, then compare.
Counting tick marks instead of spaces on a number lineCount the jumps between marks.
Ordering the wrong wayRead whether the question asks least to greatest or greatest to least.

faq.q: Why add a zero to compare decimals?
faq.a: 0.5 and 0.50 are equal. Writing both numbers with hundredths makes it easy to compare the digits.

items.q: Which point is at 0.3?
items.e: Each space is 1 tenth. 0.3 is 3 tenths, so count 3 spaces from 0. That is point B.

items.q: Which point is at 1.8?
items.e: Find 1 first, then count 8 spaces past it. Each space is 1 tenth, so 1.8 is at point D. (0.8, without the whole, would be 8 spaces from 0.)

items.q: Which point is at 0.8?

sets.title: Fractions and decimals as distances from 0

items.q: The red dot is at 12. Name the same point in sixths.
items.e: Each half is split into 3 small spaces, so there are 6 spaces from 0 to 1. Count the spaces from 0 to the dot: 3. So 12 = 36.

items.q: The red dot is at 23. Name the same point in sixths.
items.e: Each third is split into 2 small spaces, so there are 6 spaces from 0 to 1. Count the spaces from 0 to the dot: 4. So 23 = 46.

items.q: The red dot is at 34. Name the same point in eighths.
items.e: Each fourth is split into 2 small spaces, so there are 8 spaces from 0 to 1. Count the spaces from 0 to the dot: 6. So 34 = 68.

items.q: The red dot is at 13. Name the same point in twelfths.
items.e: Each third is split into 4 small spaces, so there are 12 spaces from 0 to 1. Count the spaces from 0 to the dot: 4. So 13 = 412.

items.q: The red dot is at 35. Name the same point in tenths.
items.e: Each fifth is split into 2 small spaces, so there are 10 spaces from 0 to 1. Count the spaces from 0 to the dot: 6. So 35 = 610.

items.q: The red dot is at 14. Name the same point in twelfths.
items.e: Each fourth is split into 3 small spaces, so there are 12 spaces from 0 to 1. Count the spaces from 0 to the dot: 3. So 14 = 312.

items.q: The grid has 100 equal squares. What fraction is shaded, in hundredths?
items.e: Each column is 110, and each column has 10 small squares. 3 columns = 3 × 10 = 30 squares, so 310 = 30100.

items.q: 710 = ?100
items.e: Tenths to hundredths: multiply the top and bottom by 10. 7 × 10 = 70, so 710 = 70100.

items.q: 210 = ?100
items.e: Tenths to hundredths: multiply the top and bottom by 10. 2 × 10 = 20, so 210 = 20100.

items.q: 60100 = ?10
items.e: Hundredths to tenths: divide the top and bottom by 10. 60 ÷ 10 = 6, so 60100 = 610.

items.q: 90100 = ?10
items.e: Hundredths to tenths: divide the top and bottom by 10. 90 ÷ 10 = 9, so 90100 = 910.

items.q: 12 = ?100
items.e: 2 × 50 = 100, so multiply the top by 50 too: 1 × 50 = 50. So 12 = 50100.

items.q: 14 = ?100
items.e: 4 × 25 = 100, so multiply the top by 25 too: 1 × 25 = 25. So 14 = 25100.

items.q: 35 = ?100
items.e: 5 × 20 = 100, so multiply the top by 20 too: 3 × 20 = 60. So 35 = 60100.

items.q: 45 = ?100
items.e: 5 × 20 = 100, so multiply the top by 20 too: 4 × 20 = 80. So 45 = 80100.
